stem:
Qadir lists every whole number from $10$ to $19$. He wants the number of times the digit $1$ is written in that list.

Which count is correct?

options.text: Count $10$, $11$, $12$, $13$, $14$, $15$, $16$, $17$, $18$, and $19$ as ten hits, treating each number that contains a $1$ as a single hit.
Say that writing the digit $1$ is what creates the list from $10$ to $19$.
Count every written $1$: one in $10$, two in $11$, and one each in $12$ through $19$, for $11$ written ones.
Use the same $11$ also as the count of how many times $1$ appears from $1$ to $100$, with no further check.

teacher.key_rationale: Each written appearance of the digit counts, so $11$ contributes two ones and the range yields eleven written ones. Counting numbers that contain a $1$ once each omits repeated digits. Reversing digit and list, or extending the same total to $1$–$100$, leaves this hinge.
